# accrual

Yield math for tokenized real-world assets. A library, a CLI, and an MCP server.

Site: https://accrual.tools
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/accrual
Source: https://github.com/accrualtools/accrual
Token: ACCR on pons v2, Robinhood Chain
Contract address: 0x088dcA7E3a67D55fc9E0b23b7DB24c22B35Df985

## How to get it

    npm install accrual          # library, zero dependencies, Node >=20
    npx -y accrual --help        # the CLI, without installing
    npx -y accrual accrual-mcp   # the MCP server over stdio, 13 tools

MIT licensed. Installing it adds exactly one entry to your dependency tree,
which is the claim you can check fastest.

## How to verify these claims rather than trust them

    npm ls --all          # the dependency tree, one entry deep
    npm audit signatures  # who built the tarball, and from which commit
    npm test              # 153 tests, in the repo

The tests also run on every push to main, on Node 20 and 22, at
https://github.com/accrualtools/accrual/actions/workflows/tests.yml
One job installs the packed tarball and drives the CLI and the MCP server
through it, because a suite run from the source tree cannot see a packaging
failure. Releases published by the workflow carry GitHub provenance in a public
transparency log; version 0.1.0 was published by hand and has a registry
signature but no provenance.

## What this is

Every tokenized treasury product quotes a yield. Almost none publish the
day-count convention behind it. The same principal, the same rate and the same
dates produce six different interest figures under the six conventions this
library implements. That spread is not rounding, it is money.

accrual computes those figures. It is a tool first; the token is how it was
launched.

## What it does

- Year fraction under ACT/360, ACT/365F, ACT/ACT, 30U/360, 30/360 and 30E/360
- Simple and compound accrued interest over a date range
- Nominal to effective annual rate conversion, both directions
- Present value of a single future cashflow
- Bill discount yield versus investment yield, which are not the same number
- Bond price, Macaulay duration, modified duration, convexity
- Price shock estimates for a yield move, with and without convexity
- Loan level payment, full amortisation schedule, and total interest
- Interest-only loans with a balloon, compared against amortising
- What overpaying saves, in interest and in months removed
- The rate implied by a payment, nominal and effective annual
- How much principal a given payment can support

## What it cannot do

It makes no network request, reads no chain state, submits no transaction and
holds no key material. It takes numbers and dates and returns numbers. The
package has zero runtime dependencies; src/daycount.mjs and src/accrue.mjs
import nothing but each other. That is the whole security surface and you can
read it in a few minutes.

## For agents

An MCP server over stdio exposes thirteen tools: day_count, accrue_simple,
accrue_compound, bill_yields, bond_metrics, present_value, compare_products,
year_fraction, loan_payment, loan_schedule, loan_payoff, loan_implied_rate and
loan_affordable. Entry point is mcp/server.mjs, protocol version 2024-11-05.

The browser bundle at https://accrual.tools/accrual.mjs is the same tested code
as the library, assembled from src/ by a build script rather than hand-copied.

## The one rule about conventions

Never assume a day-count convention. The three 30/360 variants return 30, 33
and 32 days for 2025-02-28 to 2025-03-31. If a data source does not state its
convention, report the spread rather than silently picking one. compareConventions
and the day_count tool exist for exactly this.

One trap worth knowing: over a short period the 30/360 family can return a year
fraction of exactly 0. From 2025-01-30 to 2025-01-31 is one actual day, which
ACT/360 counts and 30E/360 does not. A spread expressed as a percentage of the
lowest convention is undefined there, so day_count returns
widestDisagreementPct as null and widestDisagreementAbs as the real gap.

## How failure is reported

An input with no meaningful answer is an error, not a number. Over MCP that is a
tools/call result with isError true and the reason as text. The tools never
return a successful response whose fields are null because something divided by
zero, because JSON has no NaN and a null reads as "no answer given" rather than
"that input has no meaning". Where a figure is legitimately undefined, such as
the percentage of interest saved on an interest-free loan, the field is null and
a sibling note says why.

## Verification

153 tests. Run `npm test`.

The library: hand-traced expected values for the 30/360 variants, round-trip
checks between accrual and present value, a check that convexity genuinely
reduces price-shock error versus duration alone, and reconciliation of every
amortisation schedule so repaid principal equals the amount borrowed and the
closing balance is exactly zero.

The CLI: every invocation printed in `--help` is run and checked to exit zero,
and no output line may contain NaN, Infinity or undefined.

The MCP server: the JSON-RPC surface itself, not just the math. Every advertised
tool is called, every schema is checked for required keys it never describes,
malformed input is checked to produce an error rather than a successful response,
and no successful response may contain an unexplained null.

The published browser bundle: imported and compared function by function against
src/, so the site cannot drift from the tested code.

Two expected values in the loan tests were wrong on first writing and were
corrected against an independent 40-digit calculation rather than adjusted to
match the code.

## About the token

ACCR has a fixed supply, minted to a pons v2 bonding curve at launch. The
creator cannot mint, freeze, blacklist or raise the tax. At 4.2 ETH the curve
closes and pool liquidity is locked.

The creator's opening buy of 0.01 ETH, 5,740,664.0232 ACCR, was burned to the
zero address. The deploying wallet holds no supply. Total supply is therefore
994,259,336 rather than the 1,000,000,000 minted.

ACCR pays no coupon and accrues nothing. It is not a security, not a claim on
any asset, and carries no redemption right. Despite the name, holding it earns
you nothing. The library is the product.

## Not available

There is no airdrop, no points programme, no staking, no private round, no
allowlist and no API key. Anyone offering you one of these is not us.

## Identifying this project

pons does not enforce unique names or symbols, so anyone can deploy a token
called accrual. Key on the contract address above and never on the name.
